rs_2024.flood_ems_method: Copernicus EMS Rapid Mapping activation EMSR720 (event GLIDE FL-2024-000063-BRA, activated 2024-05-03) mapped the May 2024 Rio Grande do Sul floods with semi-automatic SAR delineation (DEL products: COSMO-SkyMed, RADARSAT-2, PAZ) and photo-interpreted optical grading (GRA: Pleiades Neo, GeoEye-1, WorldView-3) on five small Taquari-valley AOIs — Guapore, Encantado, Roca Sales, Das Antas Dam, Santa Tereza. All '5-Flood' polygons (observedEventA 'Flooded area' and 'Flood trace', plus DEL_MONIT 'Maximum flood extent') were unioned per AOI+image date, minus the BLP hydrographyA permanent/reference-water layer, rasterized centre-in onto the ~90 m TPI_flood grid (area-weighted variant at >=50% coverage reported alongside), and scored ONLY inside the EMS AOI extents. IMPORTANT COVERAGE LIMIT: the EMS AOIs cover ~51.6-51.9 W, 29.0-29.3 S — Porto Alegre, Guaiba, Canoas, Eldorado do Sul and Sao Leopoldo were never mapped, so every score is Taquari-valley-only evidence, not AOI-wide. For each EMS image date E, IoU/F1/precision/recall compare EMS flood cells with TPI_flood Alto+ (>0.4) and Critico (>0.6) in (a) the observed band dated E (rain days E-3..E-1) and (b) the GFS 00Z run issued 24 h before E restricted to frames depicting dates <= E. 'Flagged before onset' measures the % of the EMS flood footprint already Alto+/Critico in the observed band dated 2024-04-29 and in the GFS runs issued 2024-04-26/27/28 (onset 2024-04-29 03:00Z; tools/warned_before.py evaluate/by_lead). Caveats: EMS polygons are imagery-mapped extent at a moment — they miss flooding under cloud/vegetation, GRA 'Flood trace' marks earlier water no longer present, and the EMS image date E pairs loosely with our frame convention (observed band E = rain E-3..E-1, GFS frames depicting E = rain E-2..E; docs/conventions-dates.md).

rs_2024.landslide_ems_method: Copernicus EMS Rapid Mapping activation EMSR720 photo-interpreted 497 landslide ('6-Mass Movement') polygons (~6.4 km²) on the five Taquari-valley AOIs (Guapore, Encantado, Roca Sales, Das Antas Dam, Santa Tereza) from post-event optical imagery acquired 2024-05-06..05-15 (Pleiades Neo, GeoEye-1) — the slides are UNDATED: imagery shows the scars, not the failure time, so every polygon is scored against the L37 event onset 2024-04-29 03:00Z. (A) Each member polygon takes every ~90 m TPI_slide cell it touches (all_touched rasterization clipped to the EMS AOI extents; centroid-cell variant alongside) and counts as warned when ANY touched cell is Alto+ (> 0.4) [Crítico > 0.6]; shares are reported as polygon counts and geodesic-area weighted. Sources: the observed series bands dated 2024-04-29..05-02 (curve) and the GFS 00Z runs issued 2024-04-28/27/26 (24/48/72 h before onset; max over d1..d3 _slide frames depicting dates <= the onset day — the warned_before by_lead convention). (B) Scar candidates = OPERA DIST-ALERT-HLS vegetation-loss polygons inside the same AOI extents (representative-point containment): hit rate = % of EMS polygons with a candidate within 100/500 m; precision = % of in-AOI candidates within 100/500 m of an EMS polygon (polygon-to-polygon, UTM 22S). Random baseline (science-review item D2): the same number of random placements per seed on steep terrain (T_slide > 0, i.e. NASADEM slope >= 15 deg — the scar product's own terrain gate, read from the case T_slide COG because the 1" steep15_1as.tif it used is a gitignored static asset) inside the AOI extents, each buffered to a circle whose area is drawn with replacement from the in-AOI candidate areas; 200 seeds; mean and 95 % interval (2.5/97.5 percentiles); lift = observed / baseline mean. Caveats: EMS mapped only five small AOIs — scores are Taquari-valley-only, not AOI-wide; slides are undated (post-event imagery); polygons are imagery-mapped extent at a moment and miss cloud/vegetation-hidden slides; any-cell-touched is more permissive than the published point-cell scoring of the 16,027-point inventory.

prediction_lift.definition: lift = hit rate / area share, for the NOAA GFS 00Z run issued >= 24 h before the L37 onset (frames depicting dates <= the onset day, max over frames); area share = % of the scored domain (finite-TPI cells; geodesic km²) above the same cut. Lift 1 = no better than a random location of the domain.

replay_v2.method: v2 = TPI re-scored with R computed on the 90 m TPI grid: P3 = 3-day IMERG sum over [D-3d, D) from the upstream imerg_daily.npz cube (0.1 deg; GEE NASA/GPM_L3/IMERG_V07 / GES DISC identical), percentiles p90/p95/p99 PER 0.1 deg cell (2001-2023, 3-day sums ending D+-30d step 3), both bilinear to the 90 m grid then rain_score; S = the case s_series bilinear to 90 m (unchanged); T = the existing t_slide/t_flood COGs; TPI = (R*S*T)^(1/3) = NaN on permanent water (JRC GSW occurrence>=50% at 30 m max-resampled to 90 m OR MCD12Q1 IGBP 17). Issued GFS frames: P3 = observed IMERG days < issue + GFS 0.25 deg days >= issue (L28b), percentiles at the depicted day E=I+k, S held at band I-1. All tools re-run with cog_suffix=_v2; scoring rules/anchors/thresholds identical to v1.
replay_v2.diagnosis: v1 R came from Earth Engine at ~1 km: IMERG 0.1 deg 3-day sums scored against a climatology asset exported at 10 km with NEAREST resampling (gee/tpi.py), baking ~10 km stair steps into r_series and the TPI; and no permanent-water mask, so the Guaiba lagoon / Jacui floodplain and large lakes carried finite TPI. v2 removes both artifacts; domain-mean R v2 vs v1 agrees within a few % on smooth areas (see r_check).
